note: FLOOR § 11's `fx-refusals`: the responses of D2 § 8.6 and § 2.2 — `503 fleet_unavailable`, `401 token_revoked`, the `db: "down"` stream that ENDS, `fleet.reload` in both forms (the second followed by re-opens the stub refuses `503` for the spans AT-D3-8 names), and a stream that ends with no `feed.close` at all — each in a separate run, on a cold start and on a client already holding `fx-snapshot-4`.

refusal_503_cold.note: AT-D3-8: `503 fleet_unavailable` on a cold start — no floor to keep.

refusal_503_warm.note: AT-D3-8: a client holding `fx-snapshot-4` whose stream is ended with no reason at 1 s, so its first poll is answered `503 fleet_unavailable`.

refusal_401_cold.note: AT-D3-8: `401 token_revoked` on a cold start.

refusal_401_warm.note: AT-D3-8: a client holding `fx-snapshot-4` whose stream is ended with no reason at 1 s, so its first poll is answered `401 token_revoked`.

db_down_cold.note: AT-D3-8 / § 9 F5 on a cold start: the snapshot answers `503`, and the stream's FIRST message is `fleet.health` with `db: "down"` and its LAST `feed.close{reason:"unavailable"}`, the stream then ENDING (D2 § 2.2).

db_down_warm.note: AT-D3-8 / § 9 F5 on a client holding `fx-snapshot-4`: the same stream — `db: "down"` first, `feed.close{reason:"unavailable"}` last, then the end.

db_down_held_open.note: AT-D3-8's Third RED, as a FIXTURE: `db: "down"` and then the stream HELD OPEN — the posture card#9287's ruling withdrew. A GREEN that stopped at the statement would pass this run; the end and the indicator after it are what fail it.

reload_unknown.note: AT-D3-8, `fleet.reload` leg one: a `feed_version` (2) this client does not know. F8's banner; a delta delivered after it changes nothing; nothing is re-opened.

reload_known_8s.note: AT-D3-8, `fleet.reload` leg two: this client's own `feed_version`, then `feed.close{reason:"reload"}` at 2 s, and every re-open refused `503` for 8 s. The first attempt on the 10 s cadence (12 s) is accepted and its first message follows.

reload_known_42s.note: AT-D3-8, `fleet.reload` leg two, the long window: re-opens refused for 42 s after the `feed.close`, so the attempts at 10, 20, 30 and 40 s are refused and the fifth, at 50 s, is accepted.

reload_never.note: AT-D3-8's Fifth RED's run: every re-open refused for 120 s after the `feed.close` — a deploy that failed inside its window. The grace ends 60 s after the `feed.close` and step 7's render follows.

drain_end.note: AT-D3-8: a stream that ends with NO `feed.close` — the deploy's drain ending a stream that missed `fleet.reload` (D2 § 2.1). F1's render at once, and no grace.

refusal_control.note: AT-D3-8's discriminating control: a `200` snapshot in the same harness, the stream healthy.

unavailable_backoff.note: § 2.2's backed-off cadence: `db: "down"` then `feed.close{reason:"unavailable"}` at 60 ms, and every re-open refused until 200 s — so the attempts come 10, 20, 40, 80 and 80 s apart — then one accepted, whose first message resets the cadence, and a second `unavailable` close whose first retry is 10 s after it again.

never_spoke.note: § 9 F19: a stream that OPENS and never delivers a message — something between PHP-FPM and the browser buffering it (D2 § 8.3 R1). The snapshot answers; the stream is silent from the start.

stalled.note: § 9 F3 `stalled`: the server ended the stream because this client stopped draining. *reconnecting*, and a re-run from step 1 on the 10 s cadence, the first attempt accepted.
